description: The Embraer 190 is Africana's workhorse for North African regional routes. Seating 96 passengers in a comfortable all-economy configuration, it connects Algiers to key Mediterranean and Saharan destinations with efficiency and reliability.

The majestic Airbus A340-600 is the crown jewel of Africana's Algiers fleet. With four powerful engines and ultra-long range, this flagship aircraft connects North Africa to the Americas and Far East in unrivalled style and comfort.

Africana's Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner brings next-generation technology to long-haul operations from Algiers. Composite materials, improved cabin pressure and LED mood lighting give passengers an elevated experience on intercontinental journeys.

A classic of aviation history, the MD-11 continues to serve Africana with distinction. Its three powerful engines and spacious cabin make it ideal for high-capacity routes, carrying a touch of golden-era aviation elegance into the modern world.

The Embraer 175 is Africana's primary regional connector in Mozambique. Perfectly sized for shorter domestic routes, it brings reliable connectivity to communities from Maputo north along the Mozambican coast.

The CRJ900 provides agile regional connectivity within Southern Africa. Its narrow-body design allows access to smaller airfields, making it ideal for serving destinations like Vilankulo and Inhambane where larger aircraft cannot operate.

With turboprop efficiency, the Dash 8 Q400 offers economical service on shorter regional hops. Its ability to operate from unpaved strips makes it invaluable for reaching remote Mozambican destinations that jets cannot serve.

C9-AFV is the first 737-800 to carry the Africana livery. Named after the airline itself, this Boeing workhorse serves medium-haul routes across Southern and East Africa, combining proven reliability with comfortable passenger amenities.

The second of Africana's 737-800 pair, C9-AFW often operates in tandem with C9-AFV to provide high-frequency service on popular regional routes. Together they form the reliable backbone of Africana's short-to-medium haul network.

The A320neo represents the pinnacle of single-aisle efficiency. With LEAP engines cutting fuel burn by 20%, C9-CAB brings environmental responsibility to Africana's short-haul operations while offering a premium business class section on key routes.

C9-CAC joins its sister aircraft C9-CAB in offering next-generation efficiency across Africa. Deployed primarily on routes to Harare, Nairobi and Johannesburg, this neo-engine aircraft sets a new standard for regional air travel.

The A330-900neo is Africana's premier wide-body, offering intercontinental range with remarkable fuel efficiency. C9-AIA connects Maputo to Singapore and beyond, featuring a thoughtfully designed cabin with lie-flat business class seats.

The crown jewel of Africana's entire fleet — the superjumbo Airbus A380. C9-AJA is Sub-Saharan Africa's first A380 operation, making history with every departure from Maputo. The double-deck widebody carries up to 510 passengers in three cabins to global metropolises.

Built from 70% composite materials, the A350-900 is a masterpiece of modern engineering. C9-AXA delivers ultra-long-range performance with a whisper-quiet cabin, ideal for Africana's overnight flights to Melbourne and intercontinental operations.

The Boeing 777-300ER is one of the most trusted long-haul aircraft in commercial aviation. C9-BAA brings proven performance to Africana's flagship routes, featuring a premium first class suite and spacious business class on intercontinental services.

Sister aircraft to C9-BAA, the second Triple Seven gives Africana high-frequency capacity on its most popular long-haul routes. Together they operate Maputo's flagship services to Dubai, ensuring daily connections to the Arabian Gulf.

The iconic Queen of the Skies in her latest evolution. C9-BQA is Africana's Boeing 747-8, combining the timeless silhouette of the hump-backed jumbo with modern GEnx engines and a stretched fuselage for maximum capacity on ultra-long routes.

The second Embraer 190 in the Maputo fleet, C9-EAB provides regional connectivity across Mozambique and neighbouring countries. Operating alongside C9-EAA, it ensures reliable twice-daily coverage on key domestic trunk routes.
